prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which designed small molecules redirect E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins.

statement.case_for: Targeted degradation turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a reaction that a molecule can be designed to trigger, so a protein can be removed instead of occupied. The effect is measured directly as degradation kinetics, ternary-complex formation and ligase dependence, and it has been reproduced across many laboratories. Round 1 gave it the broadest base on the committee (three first places, seven rankings), and Aili, Aqvist and I already agree on Crews and Deshaies. After reading the exchange I have moved my third name from Handa to Ciulli. That gives one coherent subject, designed degraders, and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work are what made the concept general and drug-like. The shared mechanism of redirecting an E3 ligase by a small molecule can still be stated in the citation without crediting the cereblon strand as a separate discovery.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so patient benefit is promised and not shown, and Somfai is right that recognition could come before the clinical record. The three-name limit still excludes Sakamoto, who shares the 2001 proof-of-concept paper, and now also Handa, Ito, Kim and Gray, whose cereblon work explained thalidomide-type drugs. Zou's point also stands that many ternary-complex structures post-date the drugs. A critic can fairly say the chemistry is sound but the pharmacology is still maturing. B057 is the cleaner prize on attribution and maturity.

responses.point: A single message about rational degrader design is easier to defend; the glue strand explains drugs found by chance, and the originators Crews and Deshaies should not be displaced.
responses.response: You have persuaded me on the structure of the citation. I argued that one citation could cover both strands, but putting Handa in the third place meant giving the same weight to a mechanism found after the drug as to the design concept, and it pushed out the structural chemistry that made degraders general. I now take Ciulli as the third name. I agree with your suggestion to let the wording mention redirecting E3 ligases generally, so that cereblon glues are not excluded by the text, without crediting them as a separate part. I still think cereblon is the more surprising chemistry, and I would want the background text to say that.

responses.point: Crews and Deshaies with Handa reads as two discoveries rather than one, leaves out Ciulli's VHL work, and the KRAS G12C work has approved drugs and a cleaner story.
responses.response: The criticism that my configuration read as two discoveries is correct, and it is why I changed the third name to Ciulli. On KRAS G12C, it was not on the shortlist, so I cannot place it in a configuration or among alternatives. On maturity, I still weigh a measured and reproduced mechanism above approval status. A drug approval shows that a molecule works in patients. It does not by itself show the chemical principle, and degradation has been measured quantitatively in cells and animals by independent groups.

responses.point: A prize before the first degrader approval risks honouring expectation, and C-N coupling has a documented record and a clean two-person attribution.
responses.response: I accept the attribution and maturity advantage of B057 and keep it as my first alternative. My disagreement is about novelty. Chemically, C-N coupling is the hard reductive elimination solved with ligand design within a class the 2010 prize already honoured, whereas induced proximity is a new way of acting on a protein. I take your timing concern seriously, but I would separate a clinical outcome from the chemistry. The reproduced principle is already established, and I would word the citation around the mechanism of degradation and not the pipeline.

responses.point: Ternary-complex structures for cereblon glues came after the drugs, and for PROTACs they remain a minority of cases, so the mechanism may be less established than the clinical story.
responses.response: This is a fair measurement point and I have no ready answer for the share of PROTACs with a ternary-complex structure. The evidence for the principle does not rest only on structure, though. Dependence on the ligase, proteasome and ligand binding, together with cooperativity measured by biophysical assays, has been shown for many degraders. VHL-based degraders are also the best-characterised case, with Ciulli's crystal structures of the VHL-PROTAC-target complex. This is another reason for me to prefer Ciulli to Handa in the third place.

responses.point: Ciulli is preferred over Handa so the citation has one subject, and cereblon and glues could be left to a later prize.
responses.response: Your reasoning on the third name was right, and I have moved to your configuration of Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. I would keep a general phrase in the citation, such as redirecting E3 ligases with designed small molecules, so that the wording stays correct if glues are recognised later.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay recognition by a few years, as Somfai argues.
Whether Sakamoto should displace Ciulli or Deshaies given the shared 2001 paper.
Whether the committee will accept citation wording that mentions E3 redirection generally while crediting the PROTAC strand.
Whether a split among B068, B057 and B022 can produce a majority of five.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent. My work on dNTP metabolism and ribonucleotide reductase is unrelated to the shortlisted candidates, and I have no listed collaboration with any of them. My colleagues' affiliations noted in round 1 are unchanged.
